summary: Geoffrey Hinton, known as the 'godfather of AI', has quit Google to speak freely about the dangers of AI, including misinformation, job displacement, and existential risks. He warns that chatbots could be exploited by bad actors and become more intelligent than humans.

claims.text: Geoffrey Hinton quit Google to speak freely about the dangers of AI.
claims.evidence_quote: Hinton, 75, said he quit to speak freely about the dangers of AI, and in part regrets his contribution to the field.

claims.text: Hinton built a neural net in 2012 with two of his students at the University of Toronto.
claims.evidence_quote: Dr Geoffrey Hinton, who with two of his students at the University of Toronto built a neural net in 2012, quit Google this week

claims.text: Hinton warned that AI chatbots could be exploited by 'bad actors' to create spambots and manipulate electorates.
claims.evidence_quote: It's able to produce lots of text automatically so you can get lots of very effective spambots. It will allow authoritarian leaders to manipulate their electorates, things like that.

claims.text: Hinton expressed concern about the 'existential risk' of AI becoming more intelligent than humans.
claims.evidence_quote: I've come to the conclusion that the kind of intelligence we're developing is very different from the intelligence we have. So it's as if you had 10,000 people and whenever one person learned something, everybody automatically knew it. And that's how these chatbots can know so much more than any one person.

claims.text: Hinton believed Google was a 'proper steward' of AI until Microsoft incorporated a chatbot into Bing, prompting Google to worry about its search business.
claims.evidence_quote: He told the New York Times that until last year he believed Google had been a 'proper steward' of the technology, but that changed once Microsoft started incorporating a chatbot into its Bing search engine, and the company began becoming concerned about the risk to its search business.

claims.text: Elon Musk said he fell out with Larry Page because Page was 'not taking AI safety seriously enough'.
claims.evidence_quote: Last month, Elon Musk said he had fallen out with the Google co-founder Larry Page because Page was 'not taking AI safety seriously enough'.

claims.text: Valérie Pisano criticized the slapdash approach to AI safety, saying it would not be tolerated in other fields.
claims.evidence_quote: The technology is put out there, and as the system interacts with humankind, its developers wait to see what happens and make adjustments based on that. We would never, as a collective, accept this kind of mindset in any other industrial field.

claims.text: Hinton was concerned that AI will eventually replace jobs like paralegals and personal assistants.
claims.evidence_quote: Hinton was also concerned that AI will eventually replace jobs like paralegals, personal assistants and other 'drudge work', and potentially more in the future.

claims.text: Google's chief scientist Jeff Dean said Google appreciated Hinton's contributions and remains committed to a responsible approach to AI.
claims.evidence_quote: As one of the first companies to publish AI Principles, we remain committed to a responsible approach to AI. We're continually learning to understand emerging risks while also innovating boldly.

claims.text: Toby Walsh said people should question any online media they see now because of AI spoofing.
claims.evidence_quote: When it comes to any digital data you see – audio or video – you have to entertain the idea that someone has spoofed it.

claims.text: A viral AI-generated image of Pope Francis in a Balenciaga puffer coat went viral in March.
claims.evidence_quote: one such image of Pope Francis in a Balenciaga puffer coat went viral in March
